page: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and a strong text processing score of 2704.0. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8311.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7989.75. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in specialized workloads. For instance, LLM text generation using a small 135M model achieves a strong rate of 268.75 tokens per second, though performance drops to a weak 8.46 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

This server profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The combination of a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and fast local NVMe SSD storage makes it well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data processing pipelines, and software compilation.

It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high 8.0 GB of memory per core. The server includes a bundled 472 GB NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage. Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and strong text processing capabilities. It also supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, enabling efficient execution of specialized vector and matrix operations. This configuration is highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and caching workloads.
